question:
A 24-year-old woman reports a 5-day history of worsening neck pain, stating that it has become too
painful to wear her necktie for work. She also describes experiencing anxiety, palpitations, and fatigue
over the past 10 days. Her medical history includes a recent 3-day episode of flu-like symptoms that
resolved spontaneously about 20 days ago. She does not smoke and occasionally consumes alcohol.
Vital signs show a blood pressure of 119/77 mm Hg and a pulse of 110/min. Physical examination
reveals warm, sweaty extremities and severe bilateral tenderness with mild swelling of the thyroid
gland, without palpable nodules. An ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia. Laboratory studies indicate
low thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated T4 and T3 levels, and an erythrocyte sedimentation
rate (ESR) of 30 mm/h. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient’s likely diagnosis?
Answer Choices: (A) Methimazole initiation (B) Antibiotics administration (C) Radioactive iodine
ablation (D) Increase dietary intake of iodine (E) Levothyroxine administration (F) Beta-blocker therapy
alone (G) Reassurance (H) Corticosteroid therapy (I) Thyroidectomy (J) Aspirin
 A. Reassurance
B. Beta-blocker therapy alone
C. Methimazole initiation
D. Corticosteroid therapy
E. Increase dietary intake of iodine
F. Thyroidectomy
G. Levothyroxine administration
H. Aspirin
I. Radioactive iodine ablation
J. Antibiotics administration
